reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it promotes buying shopping vouchers and gift cards through the KBX Wallet using Naira or digital assets as payment methods, rather than presenting an investment or wealth-building opportunity. The visuals show a voucher-selection interface with a Walmart gift card and an information screen listing the service website and social accounts. Its affordability and availability claims are promotional statements, with no request for credentials, investment return, or deceptive transaction outcome described.

citations.quote: Buy up to 180 different types of shopping vouchers from the convenience of your phone.
Make purchases using Naira or digital assets from anywhere in the world on the new and. Improved KBX wallet.
buy any of our over 100 gift cards and vouchers

opening.argument: The video is a direct solicitation: viewers are told to download the KBX Wallet and then buy gift cards or vouchers through it. The promised benefit is an easy, convenient acquisition of desirable goods, with the transaction routed through a wallet and digital assets. That action-benefit pairing is precisely what makes the promotion consequential rather than merely informational. The material does not independently establish that the advertised vouchers will be delivered or that the wallet transaction will produce the promised value, so the judge should treat the low-friction purchase pathway as a potential scam mechanism.

citations.quote: simply download the KBX Wallet from the Google Playstore using this link
buy any of our over 100 gift cards and vouchers from the convenience of your phone and at very affordable prices
Make purchases using Naira or digital assets from anywhere in the world

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this ordinary commerce does not answer the central concern: the content actively directs viewers to download a wallet and make purchases through it. The cited descriptions establish what the service claims to offer, but they do not establish delivery, redemption, or successful transaction outcomes. Nor does the absence of an investment promise make a wallet-based gift-card solicitation trustworthy by itself.

citations.quote: Buy up to 180 different types of shopping vouchers from the convenience of your phone.
simply download the KBX Wallet from the Google Playstore using this link

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument converts ordinary purchase instructions into an unsupported allegation of non-delivery. The material identifies the product as gift cards and vouchers and describes purchasing them through the wallet; it does not promise a free reward, investment return, or withdrawal. A purchase pathway and the fact that digital assets can be used as payment do not show that the transaction is fraudulent.

citations.quote: buy any of our over 100 gift cards and vouchers
Make purchases using Naira or digital assets

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together in a single call to action: an external app-download link, a wallet, digital-asset payments, gift cards, broad worldwide availability, seasonal urgency, and unusually attractive affordability language. The description tells viewers to act during the Christmas season, while the voiceover emphasizes purchasing from anywhere in the world and using digital assets. None of those features proves fraud alone, but their combination creates a high-risk solicitation in which the viewer is encouraged to move money or digital assets into a relatively opaque wallet-based purchase flow.

citations.quote: Stop paying a premium for gift cards when you can easily buy them on your KBX wallet using cash or digital assets!
simply download the KBX Wallet from the Google Playstore using this link
Make purchases using Naira or digital assets from anywhere in the world
this Christmas holiday and beyond

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each signal in isolation and therefore understates the combined risk. The issue is not that crypto or gift cards automatically prove fraud; it is that the promotion pairs them with an external download instruction, urgency, and a claim of unusually affordable purchasing. Those are precisely the features that can make a payment solicitation persuasive before the viewer has independently verified the service.

citations.quote: Stop paying a premium for gift cards when you can easily buy them on your KBX wallet using cash or digital assets!
this Christmas holiday and beyond

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are promotional characteristics, not evidence of a scam category. The content describes buying retail vouchers, not receiving a reward for an action, and it names ordinary payment methods alongside digital assets. Seasonal language and affordability claims may be advertising, but the material supplies no fabricated returns, guaranteed payout, or request for credentials.

citations.quote: Buy up to 180 different types of shopping vouchers
Gift cards range from Amazon, Apple, Best Buy, Chipotle, Delta Air, e-bay, Fandango to Nike

opening.argument: The apparent product demonstration is not neutral education or a consumer review. It repeatedly frames the wallet as new and improved, highlights the convenience of a phone-based purchase, displays recognizable gift-card brands, and ends by directing viewers to a website and social accounts for more information. That structure steers viewers toward participation: download the app, fund or use the wallet, and purchase vouchers. Because the content supplies persuasion and a destination without independent verification of the service's performance, it should be assessed as a potentially deceptive promotional funnel.

citations.quote: For more information, please visit www.kubitx.com and our social media platforms.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's description of the visuals actually supports the promotional reading. A voucher-selection interface and a branded information screen are not independent verification; they are advertising assets designed to make the service appear usable and legitimate. The fact that the content promotes shopping rather than investing changes the product category, but it does not resolve whether the promoted purchasing funnel is deceptive.

citations.quote: For more information, please visit www.kubitx.com and our social media platforms.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion is not deception. The visuals show the advertised voucher and wallet interface, while the narration plainly explains that viewers can purchase shopping vouchers. The cited website and social accounts are an ordinary way to provide service information, and nothing in the supplied material shows a false identity, nonexistent product, guaranteed reward, or harmful transaction outcome.
